messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) the melting/freezing point of pure water drops to roughly **–2 °C**.  
This is because the phase diagram of water shows that the solid–liquid equilibrium line slopes downward as pressure decreases; at 10 kPa the equilibrium temperature is about two degrees below the normal 0 °C freezing point.
